review.tagline: Autonomous pentester that exploits web apps and APIs using source code analysis
review.summary: Shannon reads a web application's source, maps attack paths, then uses browser automation and command-line tools to run real exploits against the running app and its APIs. Only findings with a working proof of concept reach the PDF, Markdown, JSON or SARIF 2.1.0 report. It runs from an npx launcher with an ephemeral Docker worker, and also ships a GitHub Action and a GitLab CI component.
review.audience: Developers and security teams pentesting apps they own, locally or in CI
strengths: Reports only exploits with a reproducible proof of concept, which cuts speculative scanner noise
Outputs PDF, Markdown, JSON and SARIF 2.1.0; GitHub Action and GitLab CI can gate on exploited findings
Bring your own key: Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Bedrock, gateways, or local Ollama, vLLM and LM Studio
Supports authenticated scans (login flows, TOTP) and resumable workspaces
weaknesses: Needs source code of the target; black-box testing is only in paid Pro and Enterprise
Actively executes exploits, so it must not be pointed at production systems
Anthropic and OpenAI cyber safeguards can interrupt scans unless you complete their verification
Claude Code subscriptions unsupported after version 1.9.0; model API costs are yours
needs: Needs Docker, Node.js 18+, AI provider API key or subscription
Models: Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, AWS Bedrock, Ollama
